text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000381 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation at every complexity level, with nearly half on low-complexity patients, but the few documented charts support the billed levels, so the record is too thin to call.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern raises concern. The 99215 share runs roughly two to three times the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with zero or one chronic condition. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include visits coded only for routine problems such as upper respiratory infection (e.g., C0214578, C0214627), urinary tract infection (C0215239) or follow-up (C0214961), which is the pattern most consistent with upcoding. Against that, the documentation does not show it. The four documented 99215 charts, including the low-complexity claims C0215223 and C0215917, recorded high MDM with time to match. Unsupported rates at 99213 and 99214 are in line with peers, and only one note claiming moderate-or-higher data review lacked a lab or test line. With records for only about 1% of claims and just four at 99215, the documentation is too thin to confirm or rule out upcoding. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, especially the acute-only visits coded J06.9, N39.0, R21 and Z09, and check whether the notes support high MDM or look templated."}
